blocks.content: An action is a plain JavaScript object that describes what happened. It always has two parts:

items: type — A string that identifies the event. This is what the reducer reads to decide which logic to run.
payload (optional) — Any additional data the reducer needs to compute the new state.

blocks.content: Here are two examples from our journal app:

{ type: "SET_ENTRIES", payload: data }

{ type: "BOOKMARK_ENTRY", payload: { id: 3 } }

items: The first action replaces the entries with data.
The second toggles the bookmark on entry 3.

blocks.content: In both cases, the type tells the reducer what to do, and the payload supplies the data it needs to do it.
Let's see how the reducer uses these actions.
